W1 (mechanism), after E010.

The setup
- The tip is E010. It is E008 (Muon on the conv filters, Lookahead/EMA, resizing 24/28/32 px at 40/30/30% of steps, batch 2000, epochs=9.5 in the code) with group 3 narrowed to 512 channels.
- It scores time 6.639 s and accuracy 0.75477. The margin over 0.753 is only 0.18 pp, so the tip is fragile for the 40-seed judgment. Any further accuracy cost must be bought back with time saved somewhere else.

Measured effects
- Compile + fused SGD: about −14% time. Accuracy is deterministic: E003 and E004 both gave 0.748633.
- Lookahead/EMA: +0.97 pp for about 0.6% more time (E005). The t^3 alpha ramp anneals both the weights and the BN buffers.
- LR floor 0.07 → 0: −0.08 pp (E009). It is redundant with the EMA.
- Muon: +0.66 pp at +4% time (E006).
- Resizing 24/28/32: −22% time and −0.59 pp (E007). Time tracks pixel share, so the run is GPU/FLOP-bound.
- Epoch cut of 0.5 with EMA on: −0.18 pp and −4.8% time (E008).
- Group-3 width 576 → 512: −4.8% time and −0.25 pp (E010). This fits a FLOP model (about 5% of conv FLOPs plus some Newton-Schulz). The accuracy cost per unit of time is about the same as an epoch cut.
- Common exchange rate: every FLOP-cutting lever costs about 0.4-0.5 pp per 10% of time. There is no free FLOP lever left.

The time model
- Fixed cost is about 0.4 s: H2D copy, eigh, pad, and the per-epoch augment and interpolate.
- The variable part, about 6.2 s, scales with pixel share × width-FLOPs.
- At about 26 ms per step the GPU is saturated, and the step has no host syncs. CUDA graphs can therefore only shave launch gaps, about 0-3%. Small-resolution phases have shorter kernels, so they gain slightly more.

The accuracy model
- My earlier bias of underestimating accuracy has eased. E008 and E010 were both hits with central points.
- Lower-resolution phases: at 20 px, group-3 maps are about 2×2 (pooling 20→10→5→2). That hurts features more than linearly. The 32 px tail also shrinks to 20%, and the final EMA anneal then happens at mixed resolutions. Train/test resolution mismatch matters most near the end.

Noise
- Accuracy is bit-identical on re-runs. Time varies by about 1-2% between runs.
- Seed std is about 0.2-0.3 pp, so the 3-seed mean std is about 0.15 pp.
- At 0.7548, the tip's 40-seed mean is roughly 85% likely to be at or above 0.75.

Unsure
- Whether CUDA graphs interact badly with the Lookahead foreach ops and the 4-CPU pin. They might also expose a CPU-bound gap I have not measured.
- Whether the 0-2 seeds sit high or low relative to the 40-seed mean.
- The best next move is probably a time-neutral accuracy gain (BN recalibration, LS or lr retune, alternating flip) to rebuild margin, then spending that margin on epochs.

forecasts.reason: Pixel share drops 0.755→0.639, which saves about 11% of time. But 20 px leaves 2x2 maps in group 3 and the 32 px tail falls to 20%, costing about 0.5-1 pp from a margin of only 0.18 pp, so it lands below 0.753.
No recipe change, so seeds 0-2 give bit-identical accuracy. I expect the held-out mean within 0.3 pp and a std of about 0.2-0.3 pp. CUDA-event timing adds a small overhead.
The GPU is saturated at about 26 ms per step with no host syncs, so graphs only remove small launch gaps, about 0-3%, which is below the 3% bar. Accuracy should be about unchanged.

cruxes: Is there any time-neutral accuracy lever left (BN-stat recalibration, LS/lr/wd retune, warm-up length) worth at least 0.3 pp? If so, it can be spent on epochs or pixels at about 0.4-0.5 pp per 10% of time.
Is the step truly GPU-bound at 4 CPUs? A per-step profile showing launch gaps above 5% would make CUDA graphs and fusion worth chasing.
Do the held-out seeds (I013) put the tip's 40-seed mean above 0.75? This decides whether the 0.18 pp margin can be spent at all.
